literal: Palmyra chariot riding, even at midnight I will think of, surely; closing they do not agree, for the simple girl, my eyes.
translation: My eyes refuse to close in sleep for the sake of this simple girl. Surely, even at midnight, I think of riding the palmyra chariot.
modern: இந்தப் பேதைப் பெண்ணின் நினைவால் என் கண்கள் மூட மறுக்கின்றன; அதனால் நள்ளிரவிலும் நான் மடல் ஏறுவதைப் பற்றியே உறுதியாக நினைக்கிறேன்.
explanation: The speaker is a lover suffering from intense longing, expressing his desperation. He states that his eyes refuse to close in sleep ('படல் ஒல்லா') because of his love for the simple girl ('பேதை'). Kept awake by this torment even in the dead of night ('யாமத்தும்'), he contemplates riding the 'madal' ('மடல் ஊர்தல்'). Riding the madal is an extreme ancient Tamil custom where a frustrated lover publicly rides a rough chariot of palmyra stems to win his love. The particle 'மன்ற' emphasizes his absolute certainty and resolve in this desperate act.
